subject: Runbook & Capacity: staged POC sizing, ownership, and KPIs
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@lumen.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runbook & Capacity: staged POC sizing, ownership, and KPIs

Thanks for the quick call today — great alignment on objectives. Recap and proposed plan below.

Goals / success criteria (as discussed):
- End-to-end latency <= 300ms p50 for single prompt generation (up to 1k tokens)
- Model output quality score >= 0.85 on your evaluation set (per provided prompts)
- Stable throughput of 50 requests/min while staying under $0.12/token cost target
- Clear observability: token-level cost, per-model latency, and error traces

POC scope & timeline:
- 3-week trial (Week 0 prep, Week 1 run, Week 2 stress & regression checks)
- Start date: May 9, 2027 — kickoff meeting proposed May 10

Capacity proposal (initial):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated to your trial) — ensures predictable latency
- Autoscaling: allow scaling from 1 -> 8 GPUs based on queued concurrency (policy to cap sustained scale for cost control)
- Burst: temporary burst up to 12 GPUs for traffic spikes (30 min window, overage alerts + approval flow)

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood: Marcus (sales) — commercial/coordination; Monica (solutions) — POC runbook & infra; Dev (infra) — autoscale policy and quotas
- LumenAI: Priya — product owner; Jordan — infra contact

Attachments: runbook-v1.pdf (draft), sizing-table.csv

Ask: Priya — confirm the success metrics above and whether the 3-week cadence works. Also confirm any hard limits on burst GPUs or cost caps you need.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0183
From: Priya Shah <pshah@lumen.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Bates <jbates@lumen.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook & Capacity: staged POC sizing, ownership, and KPIs

Thanks Marcus — this is helpful.

A few clarifications:
- The 300ms p50 is our stretch goal; p95 under 800ms is acceptable for initial run. We'll judge quality primarily on the evaluation prompts we shared.
- Cost cap: we cannot exceed $8,000 for the POC. Can you confirm the proposed autoscaling/burst plan will not go beyond that without an explicit approval step?
- Telemetry: we'll need a way to export token-level billing to our S3 and ship logs to our Splunk stack. Is that supported during trial?

Jordan will loop in our security SME if we need to share any IP/keys.

If that all looks good, we can confirm the kickoff May 10 at 10am PT.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Product, LumenAI
pshah@lumen.ai
(212) 555-0124
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@lumen.ai>, Jordan Bates <jbates@lumen.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook & Capacity: staged POC sizing, ownership, and KPIs

On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 2:36 PM Priya Shah <pshah@lumen.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Marcus — this is helpful.
> 
> A few clarifications:
> - The 300ms p50 is our stretch goal; p95 under 800ms is acceptable for initial run. We'll judge quality primarily on the evaluation prompts we shared.
> - Cost cap: we cannot exceed $8,000 for the POC. Can you confirm the proposed autoscaling/burst plan will not go beyond that without an explicit approval step?
> - Telemetry: we'll need a way to export token-level billing to our S3 and ship logs to our Splunk stack. Is that supported during trial?

Answers/comments:
- Autoscaling & cost control: we will enforce a hard budget alert at $6,500 (internal) and a configurable spending cap that prevents further scale at $8,000 unless Priya explicitly approves via the console. We'll surface pre-approval prompts for any burst beyond baseline.
- Proposed instance sizing: baseline 2x A100 (reserved), min 1, max 8 GPUs autoscale; burst to 12 allowed but requires two-step approval (Slack + web confirmation). Burst sessions are limited to 30 minutes and flagged in usage exports.
- Telemetry: we can export token-level billing and per-request traces to an S3 bucket (we'll request write ACL). Splunk forwarding can be configured via our event webhook; will need a URL and token from Jordan.
- Security: we will not require any customer keys in prod; we can provide a temporary scoped API key for the POC and rotate it post-trial. SOC2 artifacts can be shared on the kickoff.

I've attached the draft runbook and a more detailed sizing table (sizing-table.csv). Dev — can you validate the autoscale policy and confirm the mechanism for enforcing the $8,000 cap (quota vs runtime guardrail)?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@lumen.ai>, Jordan Bates <jbates@lumen.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runbook & Capacity: staged POC sizing, ownership, and KPIs

Thanks all — agree on the plan.

Confirmed items:
- POC start: May 10, 2027; kickoff 10:00am PT (calendar invite attached: kickoff-invite.ics)
- Budget guardrail: we will block autoscaling beyond $8,000 and surface escalation to Priya/Jordan if the system hits $6,500.
- Telemetry: Monica will share S3 write specs and the Splunk webhook template ahead of kickoff.
- Deliverables by end of trial: performance report (latency, throughput), quality eval (scoring vs your prompts), cost breakdown and suggested production configuration.

Action items:
- Priya/Jordan: confirm S3 bucket name and provide Splunk webhook token before May 9
- Dev: confirm implementation of quota block and push sizing table to the POC env by May 8
- Monica: final runbook v1.1 to be uploaded to the drive and linked in the kickoff notes

Thanks — looking forward to kicking this off.

Regards,
